name: Brooke Ellison

biography.name: Brooke Ellison

background.family: Lives with her parents and younger brother; family members are affectionate but compare achievements frequently.
background.finances: Affluent household with extensive travel, new devices, and paid activities readily available.
background.geography: An affluent neighborhood in Austin, Texas.
background.cultureLanguages: English-speaking; family traditions center on vacations, birthdays, and public celebrations of milestones.
background.school: Private secondary school with small classes and many extracurricular options.
background.accessOpportunities: Adults can arrange transport and instruction easily. Brooke often learns about an opportunity through a parent before seeking one herself.

timeline.story: Brooke loved wearing a sparkly dress to family dinners and asking everyone to watch her jump from the lowest stair. She also spent long periods quietly fitting animal puzzles together. When adults stopped watching a performance, she sometimes began again more loudly instead of choosing a different game.

She joined gymnastics after seeing photographs of an older cousin with medals. She liked the matching outfit and learning a cartwheel but complained about repeating basic exercises. A ribbon from a casual school event stayed pinned above her bed much longer than the pictures of the exercises themselves.

Brooke became interested in drawing bedrooms with huge windows and closets. Her mother bought a set of drawing materials, which she used intensely for several weeks. She then moved on to collecting miniature toys. At school she enjoyed reading aloud when she already knew every word in the passage.

She asked to join a demanding activity because successful older students seemed admired. The early sessions involved waiting, practice, and ordinary mistakes, and she soon wanted to stop. Her parents disagreed about whether to insist. She remembers feeling watched by them more than remembering the activity itself.

Brooke started saving photographs of elaborate apartments, expensive trips, and celebration dinners. She said she wanted a life people noticed. She helped at one school sale, but her strongest memory is choosing what to wear; she cannot remember whether taking payments or setting up tables interested her more.

She attended several short programs suggested by adults and liked meeting students from other schools. She described some sessions as inspiring at the time but rarely continued their projects afterward. Her favorite continuing activity was taking long walks with a friend, which she did not consider impressive enough to mention often.

Brooke wants substantial income, a beautiful apartment, and visible recognition in adulthood. When asked what work toward those things she enjoys now, she gives broad answers and changes examples. She recently quit organizing a student event after two meetings. She still reliably helps her brother rehearse presentations when he asks privately.

response.branchReason: Her reliable voluntary behavior is giving her brother specific presentation feedback. This provisional teaching exploration has more activity evidence than the broad wish for prestige; it does not assume she already wants a classroom or young-child setting.
response.financialAssumptions: She explicitly imagines an expensive beautiful apartment, frequent travel, celebration dinners and recognition. Premium lifestyle options represent that stated aspiration even though career activity preferences are unsettled. Clothing and entertainment follow her interest in appearance and visible experiences; savings is a tentative generous assumption, not current behavior. No education preference is specified.

responseRationales.evidence: She briefly enjoyed puzzles and a cartwheel, but has no enduring account of chosen construction, repair, production, delivery, fish care or emergency work. Resources and program access do not establish interest in these tasks.

Short adult-arranged programs were called inspiring but their tasks are unspecified and rarely continued. No concrete evidence establishes interest or aversion in biomedical, environmental, chemical or astronomical investigation.

She used bedroom drawing materials intensely for weeks, collects interior images and describes visual preferences, supporting drawing interest with uncertain durability. Wanting to be watched or recognized is not evidence of wanting to compose, dance, sing, write or edit movies.

She reliably gives her brother specific rehearsal feedback privately, making teaching a plausible interest. Repetitive beginner exercises were disliked, so exercise instruction may be unappealing. Other support, therapy, childcare, volunteering and sports tasks are uncertain rather than inferred from sociability.

Financial abundance and recognition are desired outcomes, not evidence of liking sales, contracts, investment, business ownership or management. She cannot remember liking the work at a sale and quit event organizing; those activities stay unsure.

Detailed budgets, comparing offers and whole-event coordination are expressly unfamiliar. No evidence supports a preference for financial records, inventory, spreadsheets, mail handling or network software work; unfinished projects are not themselves proof she dislikes them.
